{{Quote|He is a truly frightening individual to behold: I on one occasion had the misfortune to encounter him while tracking a group of independent bounty hunters through the infamous fog banks of Hewl's Karap Valley: you can imagine my surprise when a pair of piercing red eyes appeared from nowhere and the fog told me to keep my distance.|P. Essex Yerac, on seeing the Filar-Nitzan Vacander|<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref>}}
The '''Filar-Nitzan''' were a [[Changeling/Legends|polymorphic]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] indigenous to the [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[DNX-N1]]. They resembled [[Color/Legends|colored]] fog or smoke, with two [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] in a color opposite that of the main body: green Filar-Nitzan had red eyes, blue Filar-Nitzan had orange eyes, and so on. The species' gaseous nature made them immune to physical damage, and it allowed them to change shape quickly enough to avoid energy attacks; they could even diffuse damage from [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolts with a difficult-to-learn skill. However, their lack of a rigid form also prevented Filar-Nitzan from easily manipulating solid objects.

Commonly considered legends, Filar-Nitzan were nearly unknown in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] beyond their [[Star system/Legends|star system]]. They featured in stories as '''cloud demons''' and '''gas devils''', entities reputed to be dangerous [[Death/Legends|killers]] and frightening apparitions. Few [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] were aware of the species' existence; those who were speculated that some four hundred individuals comprised the species' entire population. Nevertheless, some Filar-Nitzan integrated into the greater [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] as infiltrators and [[Spy/Legends|spies]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|As a Filar-Nitzan, he can waft into almost any installation undetected once any ventilation monitors have been rendered inoperable.|P. Essex Yerac, on the Filar-Nitzan Vacander|<ref name="AIR" />}}
[[File:Vacander.png|thumb|left|200px|Filar-Nitzan could sift their bodies through tight spaces, such as ventilation shafts.]]
The Filar-Nitzan were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of gaseous [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings<ref name="AE" /> who looked like puffs of smoke with wisps that wafted from a central mass. Two distinct [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] floated within the billows of the main body.<ref name="AIR" /> The [[Color/Legends|coloration]] of the central body and eyes varied widely,<ref name="AE" /> but in general, the two parts had complementary hues. For instance, Filar-Nitzan with green, blue, or yellow bodies had red, orange, or purple eyes, respectively.<ref name="CSWE I 272" /> Filar-Nitzan could hide their eyes if necessary. Members of other species generally found the smokey beings' appearance frightening.<ref name="AIR" />

Filar-Nitzan were capable of [[Changeling/Legends|shifting]] into various forms<ref name="SS">{{JournalCite|12|Shape-shifters}}</ref> and controlling their relative density. For instance, Filar-Nitzan were able to condense their gaseous bodies as small as 0.3 square [[Meter/Legends|meters]], or as thin as 2.1 square meters.<ref name="AE" /> The ability allowed them to sift through small openings, such as ventilation shafts.<ref name="AIR" /> Filar-Nitzan were impervious to melee attacks and other physical damage but vulnerable to energy-based injury. Filar-Nitzan who had been trained in energy diffusion had the ability to dissipate some of the damage caused by energy weapons or fire and lessen its impact. However, when confronted with a fast-moving attack, such as a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolt, a Filar-Nitzan could simply avert gas from the body so that the potentially lethal blast passed through empty space and caused no damage in the first place.<ref name="AE" />

The species' form gave them a serious handicap when trying to interact with solid objects; only with extreme effort was a Filar-Nitzan able to handle even a small solid object. They were also slow; an individual wafted about at about half the rate of an average [[Human/Legends|Human]] at a run. Nevertheless, their slow, steady movement was completely silent, a fact that made Filar-Nitzan extremely stealthy.<ref name="AE" /> Their diffuse nature also made them difficult to detect by beings used to dealing only with solid creatures. Filar-Nitzan had both male and female [[Gender/Legends|sexes]],<ref name="AIR" /> and they possessed genetic material that made [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] them possible.<ref name="GATORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref>

==Society and culture==
Filar-Nitzan could express emotions with their eyes. At least one Fllar-Nitzan had a name: this specimen, [[Vacander]], was calm and peaceable by nature.<ref name="AIR" />

==History==
The [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the Filar-Nitzan was a largely unexplored [[Planet/Legends|planet]] known as [[DNX-N1]]. The world had been charted by outsiders by the end of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and it became part of the region known as [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the Galactic Civil War, [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] knew of the species and suspected that the Filar-Nitzan did not number more than four hundred individuals.<ref name="AE" /> After the transition from the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] who studied [[Alien/Legends|alien]] life had not changed their estimate.<ref name="CSWE I 272" />

==Filar-Nitzan in the galaxy==
{{Quote|The Fliar-Nitzen infiltrator Vacander presents a special threat to the Alliance: his very nature as a gaseous being makes him difficult to detect and even harder to stop.|P. Essex Yerac, on the Filar-Nitzan Vacander|<ref name="AIR" />}}
Filar-Nitzan were exceedingly rare in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], and most beings had never heard of the species, let alone encountered one of its members.<ref name="AE" /> The few who had met a Filar-Nitzan generally found the experience harrowing, and stories from such interactions used terms such as "cloud demons" and "gas devils" to describe the species, terminology that led most non-Filar-Nitzan to dismiss the tales and to consider the gaseous beings pure myth.<ref name="AIR" /> Similarly, the Filar-Nitzan's shape-shifting abilities subjected them to common prejudices that painted polymorphic species as dangerous [[Death/Legends|killers]].<ref name="SS" />

A few Filar-Nitzan made their way beyond their home [[Star system/Legends|system]]. For instance, the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] of the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] kept at least one Filar-Nitzan specimen in captivity at the planet's [[Malio Preserve Units]]; they eventually cloned the species after much difficulty.<ref name="GATORW" /> Filar-Nitzan could be found on [[Keyorin]], a lawless world in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="UW">{{InsiderCite|89|Underworld: A Galaxy of Scum and Villainy}}</ref> The Filar-Nitzan's gaseous nature allowed them to waft through security systems created for solid beings, a fact that made the species ideal infiltrators and [[Spy/Legends|spies]].<ref name="AE" /> Vacander was one such Filar-Nitzan; during the Galactic Civil War, he was considered a major threat to the Rebel Alliance. [[Lieutenant Colonel/Legends|Lieutenant Colonel]] [[Palpatine Essex Yerac]] submitted a report on Vacander to the Alliance [[SecuriDex]] that detailed Vacander's known dealings with the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and its allies.<ref name="AIR" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Filar-Nitzan Vacander appears in the sourcebook ''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]'', written by [[Craig Robert Carey]], [[J. P. Pietrzak]], [[Bill Smith]], and [[Trevor J. Wilson]]. The book was published by [[West End Games]] in [[1995]] as part of the ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' line. Vacander's entry includes game statistics to allow gamemasters to create new Filar-Nitzan characters; the game rules establish the species as fairly clumsy, physically weak, and inept with technology, yet intelligent and perceptive.<ref name="AIR" />

Filar-Nitzan have a smaller pool of dice from which to assign various scores than that available to most other sentient species. In contrast, the species receives special abilities to allow them to avoid or lessen damage, although these powers are expensive to improve. The book suggests that players of the [[roleplaying game]] not be allowed to portray Filar-Nitzan characters. The illustration for the entry was provided by [[Matt Busch]].<ref name="AIR" />
